---
title: "Public Finance"
description: "Fiscal federalism, municipal finance, taxation, subsidies, and government expenditure"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

Public finance is the skeleton key to understanding the Indian state. I research fiscal federalism — how money flows between the Union and state governments — municipal finance, the politics of taxation, and why India's fiscal architecture shapes everything from infrastructure to welfare.

::: {.topic-hero}
::: {.topic-hero-card}
### Key stat

Urban areas contribute 60% of India's GDP, yet the total self-generated revenue of all municipal corporations combined is merely 0.4% of GDP. There will be no Viksit Bharat without decent cities.
:::

::: {.topic-hero-card}
### Big idea

We need a [Regulatory Responsibility Act](../big-ideas.html) on the lines of the FRBM Act — a law for regulatory discipline, not just fiscal discipline.
:::

:::

## Related Ideas & Notes

::: {.idea-card}
### Industrial Policy has become a religion
China is its prophet, and even its mistakes are seen as masterstrokes. Industrial policy overlooks the information problem — governments don't know enough to pick winners consistently. [Read more →](../big-ideas.html)
:::

::: {.field-note-card}
Of 100 rupees earned by the government, 61 rupees in Pakistan, 66 rupees in Sri Lanka, and 25 rupees in India go into paying interest (not principal) on existing loans. Feldstein's warning is relevant: "Fiscal deficits are like obesity. You can see your weight rising on the scale before your health suffers."

[More Field Notes →](../field-notes/index.html#public-finance)
:::
